messages.text: Hey. You don't have to figure everything out right now.
I hope you've been kind to yourself today. Even a little.
Whatever you're doing, you can take one soft breath first.
Some things can wait. You're allowed to be one of them.
You don't have to earn a moment of peace.
Just checking in. No need to do anything.
I hope something unexpectedly nice happens to you today.
It's okay if today is just an ordinary day.
You can put the weight down for a moment. It'll still be there.
There's no hurry in this particular second.
Your shoulders are trying to become earrings again.
Quick question. Have you blinked recently?
I think your chair has seen enough of you for today.
If thoughts had legs, yours would need tiny running shoes.
Somewhere, a cloud is changing its mind. Nobody minds.
You look busy. I'll pretend I wasn't here.
A very important announcement: nothing. Carry on.
Your eyebrows have been working hard. Tell them thanks.
Somewhere, a duck is having a perfectly normal day.
I was going to say something wise, but I forgot. Anyway, breathe.
Notice your feet. They're still down there.
One breath in. One breath out. That's enough.
Unclench your jaw. Let your tongue rest.
Look at something that isn't a screen.
Can you hear the quiet underneath everything?
Let your shoulders fall a little.
Feel the air touching your face.
You don't need to fix this moment. Just notice it.
Take a breath that belongs to nobody else.
For five seconds, there's nowhere else you need to be.
Welcome back. Take your time settling in.
Hi again. Take a breath before you dive in.
You're back. Start slowly, there's no rush.
Good to see you. The work can wait one more breath.
Welcome back. Be gentle with the first hour.
Whatever today has been, you're still here. That counts.
Be as patient with yourself as you'd be with a friend.
A small pause is still a pause.
You've done more than you've noticed.
It's fine to go slowly. Slow still gets there.
Someone, somewhere, is glad you exist. Probably several someones.
Your to-do list can wait while you take a minute.
You're allowed to be unfinished.
Today doesn't have to be impressive.
Rest isn't a reward. It's part of the work.
Soften your voice toward yourself for a moment.
You can start again from right here.
Nothing needs your answer this second.
Kind words count, even when you say them to yourself.
Let this be a gentle minute.
The hardest thing on your list is allowed to wait for a snack.
You're doing okay. Really.
Hold the day lightly. It doesn't need a tight grip.
A glass fills one drop at a time. So do most things.
You made it to this minute. That's something.
Quick check: are you a person or a very focused shrimp?
I dropped by. Get it? Sorry.
Your tabs are multiplying. I counted. Okay, I didn't.
If your cursor could sigh, it just did.
Somewhere, a goldfish is forgetting something too. You're in good company.
Gravity is working hard on your shoulders. Rebel a little.
This is a drop. It does nothing. Impressive, right?
Please enjoy this complimentary tiny interruption.
Fun fact: you can stretch while pretending to look for something.
Your keyboard has been touched a lot today. Give it a moment.
I'm a small drop with no important news.
Be honest: how many windows are open? Don't say. Just feel it.
A penguin walked past your desk. Probably.
The mug doesn't refill itself, but you can.
Hello from inside your computer. It's cozy.
Your posture called. It left a long voicemail.
Splash. That was me. Carry on.
Is it too late to become a lighthouse? Asking for you.
The internet will still be there. It's very reliable that way.
If your chair could talk, it would ask for a day off.
Feel the weight of your hands on the desk.
Listen for the farthest sound you can hear.
Soften the space between your eyebrows.
Wiggle your toes. Nobody will know.
Where are your shoulders right now? Just ask them.
Let your eyes rest on the farthest thing in the room.
Notice the temperature of the air on your hands.
Roll your neck slowly, once each way.
What's one thing you can see that you hadn't noticed today?
Feel your back against the chair. It's holding you.
Let one breath out a little slower than usual.
Drink some water, slowly. Taste it.
Listen to the quiet that follows a single drop.
Rest your hands open on your lap for a moment.
Look out of a window, if there is one.
Name three things you can hear. Then carry on.
Stand up for ten seconds. That's the whole task.
Feel your feet, and the floor holding them.
Unfurl your fingers. They've been curled for a while.
Watch a ripple end: notice how still it gets.
Welcome back. Water first, then everything else.
You're back. Your place is saved.
Hello again. Start with something small.
